description: Drive the wallet CLI the way a user does and keep the proof. Use to verify a withdrawal, a refused overdraft or the version line.
intro: The wallet is a CLI. Each drive runs the real command in a subprocess and keeps its transcript. Read features/README.md, then the file of the feature.

launch.text: The wallet is a short-lived CLI: there is no server to keep alive. Launch checks once that the package imports.

doctor.text: The doctor runs the version command. It reads nothing else and writes nothing.

drive.text: Each drive runs `python3 -m wallet` in a subprocess, from the repo root, and checks the exit code and the output.

evidence.text: Each drive writes one transcript file for each step: the command, the exit code and the output.

cleanup.text: Cleanup removes the scratch state folder of the run. It never removes the evidence.

preconditions: Run the commands from the repo root.
Python 3.9 or later is on PATH as python3.

drive.withdraw:
out="$(python3 -m wallet withdraw 10 3)"
printf 'python3 -m wallet withdraw 10 3\nexit 0\n%s\n' "$out" > "$EVIDENCE/withdraw-ok.txt"
test "$out" = 7
set +e
err="$(python3 -m wallet withdraw 10 11 2>&1)"
code=$?
set -e
printf 'python3 -m wallet withdraw 10 11\nexit %s\n%s\n' "$code" "$err" > "$EVIDENCE/withdraw-refused.txt"
test "$code" = 3
grep -q refused <<<"$err"

features.name: Withdraw money
features.summary: A user withdraws an amount from a balance with the CLI. The CLI prints the new balance, or it refuses an amount above the balance with exit code 3.

sub_features.text: debits an amount within the balance and prints the new balance.
refuses an amount above the balance, with exit code 3 and a `refused` line.

entry_points: Run `python3 -m wallet withdraw BALANCE AMOUNT` in a terminal.
gotchas: The amounts are whole numbers. A decimal amount is a usage error (exit code 2), not a refusal.

control.description: Delete the overdraft guard of the wallet.
